name: Norpropoxyphene
summary: Norpropoxyphene is a major metabolite of the opioid analgesic drug dextropropoxyphene, and is responsible for many of the side effects associated with use of this drug, especially the unusual toxicity seen during dextropropoxyphene overdose.

pharmacology.text: It has weaker analgesic effects than dextropropoxyphene itself, but is a relatively potent pro-convulsant and blocker of sodium and potassium channels, particularly in heart tissue, which produces prolonged intracardiac conduction time and can lead to heart failure following even relatively minor overdoses.

uses.text: The toxicity of this metabolite makes dextropropoxyphene up to 10 times more likely to cause death following overdose compared to other similar mild opioid analgesics, and has led to dextropropoxyphene being withdrawn from the market in some countries.

sideEffects.en: It builds up with repeated use and can disturb the heart's electrical conduction, causing dangerous rhythms. Naloxone reverses opioid effects on breathing but not this effect on the heart.
sideEffects.zh: 它會隨反覆使用而累積，可能擾亂心臟的電傳導，造成危險的心律。納洛酮能逆轉鴉片類對呼吸的抑制，但無法逆轉這種對心臟的作用。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它会随反复使用而累积，可能扰乱心脏的电传导，造成危险的心律。纳洛酮能逆转鸦片类对呼吸的抑制，但无法逆转这种对心脏的作用。

fact.en: This metabolite, not the parent drug, is blamed for most of the heart toxicity that led to dextropropoxyphene being withdrawn in Europe and the United States around 2009 to 2011.
fact.zh: 導致右旋丙氧芬在 2009 至 2011 年間於歐洲與美國撤市的心臟毒性，大多被歸因於這個代謝物，而非母體藥物本身。
fact.zhHans: 导致右旋丙氧芬在 2009 至 2011 年间于欧洲与美国撤市的心脏毒性，大多被归因于这个代谢物，而非母体药物本身。
